title: Your Body Is Glowing Right Now and You Can't See It

scenes.text: Your body is glowing right now. You just can't see it.
In 2009, Japanese scientists put five volunteers in a pitch-black room with an ultra-sensitive camera.
The photos showed every one of them giving off visible light, mostly from the face and cheeks.
It's about a thousand times too faint for your eyes to pick up.
The glow rises and falls through the day, peaking in the late afternoon and fading late at night.
It comes from your metabolism. Chemical reactions inside your cells throw off tiny flashes of light.
So you really do light up a room. Your eyes just aren't good enough to catch it.

description:
Your body gives off visible light, about a thousand times too faint for human eyes to see.
In a 2009 study, scientists photographed volunteers in total darkness and found the glow strongest on the face, peaking in the late afternoon.
It comes from chemical reactions in your cells.
What would you do if you could see it?
